newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits steady to easier before PPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits steady to easier before PPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were steady to easier in thin trade with most traders sidelined before today's issue of the U.S. May producer price index (PPI) and April business inventories data, dealers said on Friday.
The U.S. producer price index for May is forecast to show a gain of 0.1 percent compared with a 0.6 percent decline reported in April.
April business inventories are expected to show a gain of 0.2 percent against March's 0.3 percent increase.
"Rates were steady to a little bit softer this morning on some position adjustments," a local dealer said.
"There was little impact from Thursday's retail sales and weekly jobless claims figures and most are sitting on the sidelines," he said.
"But some people are waiting for possible direction from today's release of the producer price index and business inventories numbers," he added.
In short dates, weekend, Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.
Among term rates, one-month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent and three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent.
Nine-months eased 1/16 percentage point to 6 5-7/8 percent and twelve-months eased 1/16 point to 6-1/8 6 percent.
